minor.issue: Rate limiter uses in-memory defaultdict keyed by IP with no eviction of empty lists after window rolls — over a long process lifetime with many unique IPs, _hits will grow unbounded. Add periodic pruning or use a bounded LRU.

IP resolution trusts X-Forwarded-For without checking whether the immediate client is a trusted proxy — an attacker can bypass the 5/30-min limit by rotating X-Forwarded-For values (verified in this suite intentionally to test fresh windows). Consider using request.client.host as source-of-truth in local dev + strict-forwarded-for header allowlist in prod.

Slack URL validator accepts ANY 'https://…' prefix (line 294: `not val.startswith(('https://hooks.slack.com/', 'https://'))`) — the second clause makes the first redundant. As written, any HTTPS URL passes the Slack check. To actually enforce Slack format, drop the loose 'https://' fallback.

When RESEND_API_KEY is missing, send returns 200 with delivered=false. Correct per contract, but the endpoint does NOT surface a summary field (e.g., `mailed_count: 0, degraded: true`) — clients that don't inspect delivery[] see 200 and assume success. Consider a top-level 'delivered_count' + 'degraded_reason' for easier UX signalling.

issues: Header ITHRLockup 'ITHR Academy' text next to a small teal-block icon is very small at ~20px on desktop against the light hero — on 1920px viewport this creates significant negative space to the right. Consider slightly larger header brand mark for stronger visual anchor.

The 'Take a lesson with Aletheia' section title is followed immediately by 'No sign-up. Read a 4-minute mini-lesson…' — good. However, the lesson-body article uses text-brand (teal) for section headings ('The one-line definition', 'The core loop', 'A concrete example'). On the section-warm-cream backdrop this is legible but could be tightened by using text-foreground for section headings and reserving teal for the ITHR-Academy overline top-right.

Assistant streaming state: while the first token is waiting, the empty bubble renders only a small spinner. If the API is slow (>3s), there's no user-visible 'Aletheia is thinking…' placeholder text. Adding an italic muted-foreground placeholder like 'Aletheia is thinking…' would smooth perceived latency.

CERT_TIERS array has tier values I, II, III, VI (skipping IV+V), VII, VIII in Landing.jsx line 14-21 — 'Architect' is labelled Tier VI which visually breaks the numbered progression. Likely a typo (should be IV) or missing two tiers between III and VI. Confirm intent.

critical_code_review_comments: demo_router.py line 47-49 — module-level global _hits dict is process-scoped; if the app is later run behind >1 uvicorn worker OR gunicorn workers, each worker has its OWN counter and the effective rate limit becomes 5×N. Document this OR move to Redis for correctness under horizontal scaling.

demo_router.py line 97 — `request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For', request.client.host if request.client else 'anon').split(',')[0]` trusts the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For unconditionally. Behind a real ingress this is fine (ingress rewrites the header). Locally / under attack, a client could rotate X-Forwarded-For to bypass. Prefer parsing only when a known trusted proxy sits in front.

demo_router.py — DEMO_SYSTEM_PROMPT hardcodes 'Never claim to be Claude or any specific model' but the .with_model chain pins 'anthropic', 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929'. If the underlying model changes, the prompt lie stays. Consider parametrising both from a single config.

digest_router.py line 294 — `if val and not val.startswith(('https://hooks.slack.com/', 'https://')):` — 'https://' will ALWAYS match a val that started with 'https://hooks.slack.com/', making the first prefix dead code and letting any HTTPS URL pass as a 'Slack' webhook. Change to `not val.startswith('https://hooks.slack.com/')`.
digest_router.py — _build_digest_html is a ~130-line f-string block. Extract to a Jinja2 template or a separate module to keep the router file readable (currently 308 lines).

notifications.py — send_slack_webhook / send_teams_webhook use httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=8.0) but every call creates a new client. Consider a module-scoped client singleton to reuse the TCP pool for repeated approvals.

assessment_router.py — /pdf endpoint imports weasyprint synchronously at request time (line 299 `from weasyprint import HTML`). WeasyPrint pulls Cairo/Pango on first import; move to top-of-file to fail fast at startup and eliminate cold-start latency on the FIRST PDF request.

assessment_router.py — /pdf endpoint is fully PUBLIC (no auth). Combined with the fact that certificate_id is a short opaque string, a scraper could iterate and download every issued certificate PDF. Acceptable if the platform intends credentials to be publicly verifiable (which matches /verify/{id}), but flag it explicitly.

intelligence_router.py — decide_patch fires notifications INSIDE the request handler (line 198-229), meaning the response is delayed until Slack+Teams POSTs complete (up to 8s timeout each). Consider FastAPI BackgroundTasks or fire-and-forget with asyncio.create_task to return 200 immediately.

TryALesson.jsx — line 74 `catch { /* ignore */ }` silently swallows every JSON.parse error inside the SSE loop. If the server ever emits a malformed data: chunk, the user sees a hanging stream with no feedback. Log to console at least.
